The '''ray''' was a [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]], predatory [[Scalefish/Legends|scalefish]] [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to the [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and, after being introduced there, Naboo's [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]]. Rays teemed around the [[Water/Legends|underwater]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], home to the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. [[Color/Legends|Blue]] in color, rays were considered fast swimmers and impressive leapers due to a pronounced crescent-shaped caudal fin located at the back of their bodies.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Ray-mee-as-food.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Rays (center) and smaller mee (at right), attempting escape from the tongue of an opee sea killer]]
The ray was a [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]], long-bodied predatory [[Scalefish/Legends|scalefish]] that possessed sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]; large, wispy frontal fins; and stubby tail fins, as well as a large, crescent-shaped caudal fin. Rays were considered to be good swimmers, thanks to the powerful caudal fin. The large head and wide [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] dominated much of the body and were able to distend to hold the [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] [[Fish/Legends|fish's]] prey. They were visually [[Color/Legends|colorful]], with blue scales, a white belly, and red-and-yellow [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="WSWFG" />

==Behavior==
The ray was one of the many prey of the [[Opee sea killer/Legends|opee sea killer]], a larger [[Ocean/Legends|sea]] creature native to the depths of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Several rays could be snatched by the [[Tongue/Legends|tongue]] of the opee as it [[Hunting/Legends|hunted]]. They were also fed upon by diving [[Aiwha/Legends|aiwhas]]. On Naboo, rays were found in the [[Naboo Abyss/Legends|Naboo Abyss]]. They were especially abundant around the [[Water/Legends|underwater]] [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], but they favored open waters and surface oceans.<ref name="WSWFG" /> Though they were attracted by the lights of Otoh Gunga, they knew by experience not to swim through the [[gelatin]]ous substance that led to the air-filled chambers.<ref name="EVD">''[[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace: The Expanded Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Both the Gungans and [[Human/Legends|Humans]], known as the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] on the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]], considered the ray an excellent sportfish, as it put up a strong fight and often made spectacular leaps from the water.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|83&ndash;84|ray}}</ref>

==History==
Rays were native to the Mid Rim planet Naboo,<ref name="WSWFG" /> and were also introduced to its [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]] as part of a Gungan colonization effort after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]],<ref name="TGF">[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier|''Star Wars'' Episode I: ''The Gungan Frontier'']]</ref> which occurred in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> They were present as [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]]; his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]; and the Gungan [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] swam down to the city of Otoh Gunga to speak with Gungan representatives.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> After the events of the Invasion of Naboo, the fish was introduced to Ohma-D'un.<ref name="TGF" />

==Rays in the galaxy==
In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], rays, along with [[Mee/Legends|mee]], [[Faa/Legends|faa]], and [[Laa/Legends|laa]], were present in a holding tank aboard the ''[[Titavian IV]]'', an exploration [[Starship/Legends|vessel]] formerly operated by the [[Intergalactic Zoological Society]] on [[Mycroft]], whose mission was to gather and catalog [[Species/Legends|specimens]] from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Rendili">[[Republic 69|''Republic'' 69]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The ray first appeared in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], along with several other creatures in the deep oceans of Naboo,<ref name="TPM" /> including other scalefish with names such as [[Doo/Legends|doo]], mee, faa, [[See/Legends|see]], laa, and [[Tee/Legends|tee]]&mdash;mirroring the real-world [[Wikipedia:Solfège|musical scale]]; i.e., "Do, Re, Me, Fa, So, La, Ti, Do." Subsequent appearances of the fish include Episode I&ndash;related materials and reference guides, including [[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary|''Star Wars: Episode I The Visual Dictionary'']], which first named the species,<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> and [[2001]]'s ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'', which expanded known fauna with its chapter on Naboo.<ref name="WSWFG" />

The ray also appears in Naboo content in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']]<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> and the game ''[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier]]''. In the latter, though not one of the animals a player can choose to take to Ohma-D'un in the [[Mantaris-class amphibious medium transport|Mantaris transport]], rays can nonetheless be seen swimming in the oceans of the moon in the game's city-view setting.<ref name="TGF" /> A ray also made a brief appearance in the [[2004]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] [[Republic 69|''Republic'' 69]], along with other Naboo scalefish.<ref name="Rendili" />
